capabilities: Format YAML metadata (tags, aliases, arrays, key ordering, timestamps, titles)
Fix headings, footnotes, and content styles like list markers, emphasis, and quotes
Normalize spacing around blocks, lists, tables, and at line ends
Transform pasted text (removing hyphens, extra blank lines, and whitespace)
Toggle and configure individual rules in settings
disambiguation: Not an error-checking code linter; it directly rewrites note content and YAML according to configurable rules.
extras: Main rule documentation lives on a separate wiki and may lag the plugin release; README warns that some rule combinations (e.g. 'Paragraph blank lines' with 'Two Spaces Between Lines with Content') conflict.
problem: Obsidian has no built-in way to automatically enforce a consistent Markdown and YAML style across notes; users must fix spacing, list markers, and frontmatter by hand.
summary: Rule-based formatter that cleans and standardizes notes: YAML metadata, headings, footnotes, spacing, content styles, and pasted text.
